According to the information and explanations given to us and based on audit procedures performed by us, undisputed dues in respect of goods and services tax, provident fund, employees’ state insurance, income-tax, and other statutory dues which were outstanding, at the year end, for a period of more than six months from the date they became payable, are as follows

default_in_repayment.text:
(a)	The Company has not defaulted in repayment of loans or other borrowings or in the payment of interest thereon to any lender.

(b)	The Company has not been declared wilful defaulter by any bank or financial institution or government or any government authority.
	
(c)	The Company did not have any term loans outstanding during the year hence, the requirement to report on clause (ix) (c) of the Order is not applicable to the Company. 
	
(d)	On an overall examination of the financial statements of the Company, no funds raised on short-term basis have been used for long-term purposes by the Company.

(e)	On an overall examination of the financial statements of the Company, the Company has not taken any funds from any entity or person on account of or to meet the obligations of its subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures.  
	
(f)	The Company has not raised loans during the year on the pledge of securities held in its subsidiaries, joint ventures or associate companies. Hence, the requi

fraud.text:
(a)	No material fraud by the Company and no material fraud on the Company has been noticed or reported during the year.
	
(b)	During the year, no report under sub-section (12) of section 143 of the Companies Act, 2013 has been filed by secretarial auditor or by us in Form ADT - 4 as prescribed under Rule 13 of Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 with the Central Government.
	
(c)	We have taken into consideration the whistle blower complaints received by the Company during the year while determining the nature, timing and extent of audit procedures.

statutory_dues.text:
(a)

The Company is regular in depositing with appropriate authorities undisputed statutory dues including goods and services tax, provident fund, employees' state insurance, income-tax, sales-tax, service tax, duty of customs, duty of excise, value added tax, cess and other statutory dues applicable to it. According to the information and explanations given to us and based on audit procedures performed by us, no undisputed amounts payable in respect of these statutory dues were outstanding, at the year end, for a period of more than six months from the date they became payable. Approximately 15% of total inflows came from Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, marking a tangible structural shift during the year.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Order u/s 73 r.w.s 50 and 122 of MGST Act, 2017 disallowing Input Tax Credit of Rs 4,00,992/- along with leyving Interest of Rs 7,35,287/ and Penalty of Rs 45,264/-, making total of Rs 11,81,544/- for the financial year 2017-18. The Company has already paid a sum of Rs 40,100/- against the said demand. The Company has filed an Appeal before the Appelate Authority on 21.10.2022 and the hearing is still pending. Meanwhile the Company has in January 2025 opted for the GST Amnesty Scheme 2024 u/s 128A of CGST Act, 2017. We have filed SPL-02 on 18.02.2025 being application for waiver of penalty and interest u/s 128A of CGST Act , 2017. Further , we have paid balance tax of Rs 3,60,892/- on 26.03.2025 via Form GST DRC -03 under GST Amnesty Scheme 2024 and now await for the approval of the same. There are no further developments in the matter.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Dy. Comm. of State Tax (Mumbai-LTU-502) , Large Tax Payer Unit - I , Mumbai.
tax_litigation.status: Order yet to be received , however the demand is removed from the GST Portal by the department.

The Company shall be filing Appeal before the Divisional Dy. Comm. of State Tax ( Appeals ) with in three months from the date of the said order. We have filed the Appeal on 26.03.2025 vide Form APL-01 and made payment of Rs 1,44,558/- being 10% of the disputed tax amount. The hearing and order is pending. There are no further developments in the matter.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Asst. Comm. Jurisdiction Ghatak 9 , Ahmedabad Range 3 , Div 1 Gujarat
tax_litigation.status: Still no further progress in the matter

operating_notes.text: Fees and commission income was ₹342.77 Cr in FY26 against ₹312.58 Cr in FY25, while fees and commission expense rose to ₹77.10 Cr from ₹30.04 Cr.
ICRA reaffirmed [ICRA]BBB+ (Positive) for the company's NCDs vide report dated August 5, 2025, with no change during Q4FY26.
Debt-equity ratio rose to 0.24 at Mar-2026 from 0.15 a year earlier; debt service coverage fell to 2.73 from 10.98.
Of the ₹227.52 Cr preferential warrant issue, ₹66.88 Cr had been received by Mar-2026 (₹61.88 Cr in Q3FY26 and ₹4.99 Cr in Q4FY26), leaving ₹160.64 Cr uncalled.
FY26 visible revenue pipeline stands above ₹50 Cr.
Allotted 1,00,000 shares at ₹239.50 on warrant conversion to promoter Prakash Kacholia, receiving ₹1.80 Cr (balance 75%), leaving 5,50,000 warrants outstanding with him.
CARE Ratings reported total preferential issue proceeds received of ₹92.80 Cr as of Sep 30, 2026.
Board approved restructuring of wealth management vertical housing under ECPL and transfer of EIML and EWAL shares.

timeline.summary: Emkay Global allotted 3.78 lakh equity shares on warrant conversion by promoters, raising ₹6.79 Cr.
Emkay Global allotted 4.15 lakh equity shares to promoter Krishna Kumar Karwa upon warrant conversion, receiving balance consideration of ₹7.46 Cr.
2026-05-15: CARE Ratings' monitoring report for Q4FY26 showed ₹66.88 Cr of the ₹227.52 Cr preferential warrant issue received, with ₹160.64 Cr still uncalled and nil deviation from objects.
On 18 May 2026, Emkay Global reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹396.30 Cr (+10% YoY) and PAT of ₹15.20 Cr (-73% YoY).
Mr. Krishna Kumar Karwa and Mrs. Priti Karwa jointly with Mr. Raunak Karwa declared holding 54,79,100 Emkay Global shares on 31-Mar-2026, with no new encumbrances.
Emkay Global allotted 1,00,000 equity shares to promoter Prakash Kacholia on warrant conversion, receiving ₹1.80 Cr.
Shareholders approved Mr. Rajesh Shah (DIN: 06390775) as Non-Executive Independent Director for 5 years, effective 19th August 2026, via remote e-voting ending 13th October 2026.
Emkay Global received NSE listing approval for 100,000 equity shares issued upon conversion of preferential warrants to promoter Mr. Prakash Kacholia.
Q2FY27 results (standalone): revenue ₹141.51 Cr (+122.6% YoY), net profit ₹29.55 Cr (against a loss of ₹2.11 Cr a year earlier).
Emkay Global Financial Services reported Q2FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹156.7 Cr and PAT of ₹31.0 Cr, up 103% and 6,100% YoY respectively.
Emkay Global reports ₹8.08 Cr utilised from preferential warrants for working capital in Q2FY27
Emkay Global approved restructuring its wealth management business by transferring subsidiaries and business undertakings to Emkay Capital Private Limited alongside a ₹30 Cr rights issue investment.
